about: The first library of the three kinds (order 92, D-186; docs/design/skills-v2.md §16): actives and passives of the sword, spear and axe, bow, shield, brawling, the saddle and any steel. Each fully specified (§15.6); written by hand, not by tools/skills2/seed-data.mjs.

skills.name: Quick Cut
skills.text: A cut thrown before the other man has settled his feet. It does not win a fight. It starts one in your favour.

skills.name: Twin Cut
skills.text: Down and back up on the same line, the second cut riding the first. The first is parried. The second leaves him bleeding.

skills.name: Heart-Seeker
skills.text: You show him the high line and go in under it, point first, for the gap between the plates.
skills.never: You cut at armour and wonder why he stays up.

skills.name: Binding Parry
skills.text: When your guard takes his blade you do not let it go. For the next exchange his steel is half yours.

skills.name: Long Thrust
skills.text: The point goes out at the full length of the shaft before he is near enough to answer. Only in the first exchange.

skills.name: Haft Sweep
skills.text: The butt end comes round low and takes his feet. A man on his back thinks only of getting up.

skills.name: Brace the Point
skills.text: If he comes at you first, he comes onto the point. You set the butt and let him do the work.

skills.name: Splitting Blow
skills.text: Both hands, the whole back, the edge brought down like a woodsman on a stump. It costs you, and it costs him more.

skills.name: Snap Shot
skills.text: Nock, draw and loose in one breath while he is still closing. One shaft, before the steel comes out.

skills.name: Pinning Shot
skills.text: Low, for the thigh. He still reaches you, but he limps the whole way and keeps limping.

skills.name: Still Breath
skills.text: Before the first exchange the world goes quiet and slow. Your hand does not shake. His does.

skills.name: Shield Bash
skills.text: The rim, then the boss, into his chest. It drives the wind out of him; later it drives him off his feet.

skills.name: Shell of Oak
skills.text: You go small behind the boards for three exchanges and let him spend himself on the wood.

skills.name: Hold the Gap
skills.text: Once you are bleeding you stop trading blows. The shield comes up, the chin goes down, and you make him come through it.

skills.name: Headbutt
skills.text: Inside his reach, the brow into the bridge of his nose. Taverns teach it. So do yards and ditches.

skills.name: Wrist Lock
skills.text: You take his weapon wrist and do not give it back. Whatever he holds, he holds it badly after.

skills.name: Hip Throw
skills.text: Hip in, arm over, and the ground does the rest. Wrestlers at fairs win sheep with it.

skills.name: Pit Grit
skills.text: Blood in your mouth makes you angrier, not slower. Men who fight for coin in pits learn this or stop fighting.

skills.name: Lance Charge
skills.text: Couched, levelled, the horse at the gallop: the weight of both of you on one point. Once, at the start.

skills.name: Wheel and Strike
skills.text: After a blow that lands you do not ride on. You turn the horse inside his reach and come again.

skills.name: Ride Them Down
skills.text: You put the horse through him. A man on foot is a hundredweight; a destrier is ten.

skills.name: First Blood
skills.text: You are quickest when the fight is newest. The first exchange is yours more often than not.

skills.name: Grey Hour
skills.text: At first light and last light, when other men squint, you see well enough. Raiders choose those hours for a reason.

skills.name: Last Stand
skills.text: At the very edge something hard and cold takes over. You fight best when you have least left to lose.

skills.name: Lamp-Fighter
skills.text: Alleys, cellars, torchlit yards. You have fought in the dark so often that the dark is on your side.

skills.name: Giant-Bane
skills.text: A bigger man is a slower man, a prouder man, a man who has never had to think. You make him think.
skills.never: You fight the strong as if they were your size.

skills.name: Bitter Lesson
skills.text: A blow that lands on you teaches you where the next one comes from. You pay for the lesson, and you learn it.
